teaser: A business plan: read the logs a company already has, draw each agent's footprint, twin and policy, and find the money first and the engineering second.
core_idea: A service that manages the cost of agentic AI by observing what already exists: an estate whose bill nobody can explain shipped from the explorer side without the villager's discipline, as the Wardley map shows, with logs, traces and invoices never read together and no owner of cost; the service installs nothing, reads the logs into a vault, draws each agent's footprint, builds a twin of the estate, writes the behaviour policy each agent was in fact running under with the enforcement column filled honestly, and maps cost and capability into one graph; the findings are the cost list, which pays, and the engineering list, which is the reason; the gaps are findings too; vaults carry capture, transformation and sealed anonymised extracts; four price levels on the RiskMandate pattern, every number a labelled assumption.

nodes.label: Cost is an engineering problem
nodes.summary: A loop, a whole context sent every call, a key with no ceiling: defects with a cause, a fix and a test, not a discount to negotiate.

nodes.label: The problem on a Wardley map
nodes.summary: Agents in production from prompts grown in sessions, on commodity model APIs billed by the token, with logs nobody reads together and no owner of cost.

nodes.label: Observe: install nothing
nodes.summary: The customer drops invoices, logs, traces, prompts and schedules into a vault they own, sealed to the service's key.

nodes.label: The footprint from the logs
nodes.summary: What each agent actually did: calls, tokens, tools, retries, loops, hours, data touched; the first thing the money attaches to.

nodes.label: The twin of the estate
nodes.summary: A graph of agents, models, keys, tools, data, owners and schedules with a cost on every edge.

nodes.label: The policy each agent was really running under
nodes.summary: Written from the footprint as an Agent Behaviour Policy with the enforcement column filled honestly; where the cost is large the policy is large.

nodes.label: Two lists, in this order
nodes.summary: The cost list pays for the engagement; the engineering list, attrition, gaps, shared components, is the reason to have it.

nodes.label: The gaps are findings
nodes.summary: An agent with no logs has no footprint, no owner and no policy; not being able to do the analysis is its first result.

nodes.label: Capture, transform, move
nodes.summary: Logs in once, every transformation a commit, the twin a vault of its own, anonymised extracts out as sealed envelopes to a benchmark vault.

nodes.label: Four levels and a share of savings
nodes.summary: Kit £50, your cost vault £250, Standard £3,000, Tailored from £9,000, or a share of the first year's reduction; all labelled assumptions.

nodes.label: What is already here
nodes.summary: The footprint method, the policy format, the connector twin, the vault tooling and the Company X-Ray pattern; not yet the analysis catalogue, the twin schema, the parsers or a customer.

quotes.text: Not being able to do the analysis is the first result of the analysis, and it is the one most companies need first.
So the service sells cost reduction, and delivers engineering opportunity, and the business model follows the second.
quotes.why: The positive frame and the business model in one line.

quotes.text: A cost review is a thing companies buy once and resent. A map of what to build is a thing they come back for.
quotes.why: Why the second list is the business.
